steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' library.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have access to React and the useState hook for managing state in your component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState. Now you can use React to create components and useState to manage state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'. Check your import statement syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import both React and useState from the 'react' library. Try again.

steps.title: Create the main BreadcrumbGenerator component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named BreadcrumbGenerator that returns null initially.
steps.hint: Define the component using either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. Make sure it returns null.
steps.seedCode:
// Import React and useState here

// Create the BreadcrumbGenerator component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named BreadcrumbGenerator is defined and returns null.
successCriteria: The BreadcrumbGenerator component is defined and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you define a component named BreadcrumbGenerator that returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check the name and that it returns null.

steps.title: Define the route tree data structure
steps.instruction: Inside your BreadcrumbGenerator component, define a constant named 'routeTree' with a sample nested route object. The object should have properties: 'id', 'name', and 'children' (an array).
steps.hint: Create a JavaScript object with nested objects inside the 'children' array to represent a route hierarchy.
steps.expectedOutcome: A 'routeTree' constant is defined inside the component, containing a sample route tree with at least one level of nesting.
successCriteria: The 'routeTree' constant exists and is an object with 'id', 'name', and 'children' properties, where 'children' is an array of similar objects.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the route tree data structure. This will serve as the foundation for generating breadcrumbs.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure 'routeTree' is an object with 'id', 'name', and 'children' properties. The 'children' should be an array, even if empty.
steps.feedbackWrong: The route tree constant is missing or incorrectly structured. It should be a JavaScript object with 'id', 'name', and 'children' properties.

steps.title: Initialize state for current path
steps.instruction: Inside the BreadcrumbGenerator component, initialize a state variable called currentPath using useState. Set its default value to an empty array.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The syntax is: const [currentPath, setCurrentPath] = useState([]);
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state initialization
const [items, setItems] = useState([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a state variable currentPath initialized to an empty array, ready to track the breadcrumb path.
successCriteria: currentPath state is declared using useState
Default value is an empty array []
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the currentPath state. This will track the breadcrumb path as users navigate.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with the variable name 'currentPath' and setting its default value to an empty array [].
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to initialize a state variable called currentPath with useState, defaulting to an empty array.

steps.title: Create helper function to find path in tree
steps.instruction: Inside the BreadcrumbGenerator component, create a helper function named findPath that takes a routeId and a tree object as parameters and returns an array of route objects representing the path.
steps.hint: You can define the function using either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. The function should return an empty array initially.
steps.expectedOutcome: A findPath function is defined inside the component, ready to be implemented with tree traversal logic in later steps.
successCriteria: The component contains a findPath function that accepts routeId and tree parameters and returns an array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the findPath helper function. This will be the foundation for traversing the route tree to build breadcrumbs.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your findPath function accepts both routeId and tree parameters and returns an array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The findPath function should be defined inside the BreadcrumbGenerator component with the specified parameters and return type.

steps.title: Create handler to update breadcrumb path
steps.instruction: Inside the BreadcrumbGenerator component, define a function named handleRouteSelect that takes a routeId parameter, calls the findPath helper with that routeId and the routeTree, and updates the currentPath state with the result.
steps.hint: The function should call findPath(routeId, routeTree) and pass the result to setCurrentPath.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a handleRouteSelect function that uses the findPath helper to update the currentPath state.
successCriteria: The handleRouteSelect function is defined, takes a routeId parameter, calls findPath with routeId and routeTree, and calls setCurrentPath with the result.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the handler that will update the breadcrumb path when a route is selected.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the handler, but make sure it calls findPath with the routeId and routeTree, and updates currentPath with the result.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handler isn't defined correctly. It should take a routeId, call findPath(routeId, routeTree), and update currentPath with the result.

steps.title: Add container div and title
steps.instruction: Inside the BreadcrumbGenerator component's return statement, replace the current null with a div element containing an h1 with the text 'Breadcrumb Generator'.
steps.hint: Return a JSX structure with a div wrapper and an h1 heading inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a div containing an h1 heading with the title 'Breadcrumb Generator'.
successCriteria: The return statement contains a div element with an h1 child displaying 'Breadcrumb Generator'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the container and title, establishing the basic structure of the component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've replaced null with a div containing an h1 with the exact text 'Breadcrumb Generator'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The return statement should be a div with an h1 inside it, not null or a different structure.

steps.title: Display the route tree structure
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your BreadcrumbGenerator component, add a <pre> tag that displays the routeTree constant to show the available routes for selection.
steps.hint: Use JSX syntax with a <pre> tag and embed the routeTree constant inside curly braces to display it as formatted JSON.
steps.expectedOutcome: The routeTree data structure will be displayed in the UI inside a <pre> tag, showing the available routes in a readable format.
successCriteria: A <pre> tag is added to the return statement that displays the routeTree constant using JSON.stringify for formatting.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully displayed the route tree structure, making the available routes visible for selection.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using a <pre> tag and displaying the routeTree constant inside it with proper formatting.
steps.feedbackWrong: The route tree structure isn't displayed correctly. Check that you've added a <pre> tag in the return statement and are showing the routeTree constant.

steps.title: Add route selection dropdown
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add a select dropdown element with options for each route in your route tree, and wire its onChange event to call handleRouteSelect with the selected route name.
steps.hint: Create a select element with options for 'Home', 'Products', 'Electronics', 'Clothing', and 'About'. Use the onChange event handler to update the current path.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Dropdown for selecting categories
<select onChange={(e) => handleCategorySelect(e.target.value)}>
  <option value="fruits">Fruits</option>
  <option value="vegetables">Vegetables</option>
</select>
steps.expectedOutcome: A dropdown appears in the UI with options for all routes in the tree. Selecting a route updates the current path state.
successCriteria: The select dropdown is present with options for each route name, and its onChange event calls handleRouteSelect with the selected value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the route selection dropdown. Users can now select different routes to see their breadcrumb paths.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a dropdown, but make sure it has options for all route names and the onChange handler properly calls handleRouteSelect with the selected value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The dropdown is missing or not properly configured. Check that you have a select element with options for each route, and that onChange calls handleRouteSelect with the selected route name.

steps.title: Display the current breadcrumb path
steps.instruction: Inside the component's return statement, add a <div> element below the existing <h1> that displays the currentPath array with route names separated by '>' symbols.
steps.hint: You can use the map method on currentPath to join the route names with ' > ' separator.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show a breadcrumb trail (e.g., 'Home > Products > Electronics') when a route is selected from the dropdown.
successCriteria: A <div> element displays the currentPath array with route names joined by '>' symbols.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully displayed the breadcrumb path. The UI now shows the hierarchical navigation trail.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're displaying the currentPath array with proper formatting (route names separated by '>').
steps.feedbackWrong: The breadcrumb isn't displaying correctly. Check that you're rendering the currentPath state and formatting it with '>' separators.

steps.title: Add visual styling to breadcrumb display
steps.instruction: Add a className 'breadcrumb' to the breadcrumb display div and map through currentPath to create styled span elements with className 'crumb' for each path segment.
steps.hint: Inside the breadcrumb display div, add className='breadcrumb' and use currentPath.map() to generate span elements with className='crumb' and key.
steps.expectedOutcome: The breadcrumb display div will have a className 'breadcrumb' and contain styled span elements for each segment in currentPath.
successCriteria: A div with className='breadcrumb' exists and maps currentPath to span elements with className='crumb' and proper keys.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added visual styling to the breadcrumb display with CSS classes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure to add className='breadcrumb' to the div and map through currentPath to create span elements with className='crumb'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The breadcrumb display doesn't have the required styling. Add a className to the div and map through currentPath to create styled span elements.

steps.title: Add default selection and final polish
steps.instruction: Add a useEffect hook to set the initial breadcrumb path to 'Home' when the component first loads.
steps.hint: Import useEffect from 'react', then add it inside your component to call handleRouteSelect with 'Home' when the component mounts.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will automatically show 'Home' as the initial breadcrumb path when it first renders.
successCriteria: useEffect is imported and used to call handleRouteSelect('Home') with an empty dependency array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The useEffect ensures the breadcrumb starts with 'Home' on initial load.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure useEffect is imported and calls handleRouteSelect('Home') when the component mounts.
steps.feedbackWrong: The initial path isn't set. Add a useEffect hook that runs once to set the breadcrumb to 'Home'.
